subject: Throughput recovery & credit proposal — Quantaforge (Aug 8 incident)
messages:
From: Alice Ng <alice.ng@quantaforge.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput degradation observed Aug 8 — logs attached

Connor —

We saw a sustained throughput degradation on Aug 8 between ~02:20 UTC and ~14:30 UTC. During that window our request throughput to the r-inference cluster serving our model dropped to ~40% of the expected baseline and some requests timed out. The impact hit a number of our production endpoints and the attached logs show the per-minute request counts and error rates.

Impact summary: 
- Window: 2026-08-08T02:20:00Z — 2026-08-08T14:30:00Z (~12.17 hours)
- Average served throughput vs baseline: ~40% (so ~60% shortfall)
- Observed spikes in 5xx and latency > 5s for ~90 minutes in the middle of the window

We need confirmation whether this incident is credit-eligible under our SLA (committed spend + throughput availability) and an estimate of the credit amount and timeline for issuance. Our billing contact (billing@quantaforge.com) is CC'd.

Attaching: quantaforge_throughput_logs.csv (per-minute counts + error codes)

Thanks,
Alice Ng
Head of Platform
Quantaforge

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Throughput degradation observed Aug 8 — logs attached

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Quantaforge's logs. Key items for the quick calc: their committed monthly spend (from HubSpot) is $180,000; SLA language ties throughput availability to a monthly credit schedule where shortfalls are prorated against committed spend based on "effective unserved capacity".

Quick derivation idea (please validate):
- Observed shortfall: 60% reduction for 12.17 hours -> equivalent unserved capacity = 0.60 * 12.17 = 7.302 hours
- Month hours baseline: 30 days assumed => 720 hours
- Pro-rata factor = 7.302 / 720 = 0.01014 (~1.014%)
- Candidate credit (pro-rata on monthly committed fee) = 0.01014 * $180,000 = $1,825 (rounded)

Notes/questions: 
- Should we discount the credit because some traffic was served at degraded performance rather than fully unavailable? The SLA has a clause capping credits at 50% of equivalent pro-rata for degraded throughput events; if we apply that cap: $1,825 * 0.5 = $912.50 -> round to $913 as a conservative issuance.
- Alternatively we can issue the full pro-rata ($1,825) if postmortem shows clear infrastructure-side root cause and no customer-side misconfig.

Marissa: recommend we run the logs through the internal credit workbook and prepare a PDF credit note. Karthik: can you confirm whether to apply the 50% degraded-cap as standard practice or escalate to finance for one-off approval?

Thanks — Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Throughput degradation observed Aug 8 — logs attached

Connor / Karthik — I ran the CSV through the standard workbook and validated the numbers. Summary attached as credit_calc_workbook.xlsx. Reconciliation highlights: 
- Verified unserved-equivalent hours = 7.30 (matches your calc)
- Baseline month hours = 720 (30-day billing window per contract)
- Gross pro-rata credit = $1,825.20
- Degraded-cap clause present in contract (section 4.2): cap = 50% of gross for throughput-degradation (not full outage). Applying cap -> $912.60

Recommendation: issue capped credit of $912.60 as an account credit to be applied to their August invoice cycle. Rationale: conservatively aligns with contract language and reduces finance churn. If leadership wants to make this whole, we can escalate but we'd need approval from Finance (I can route).

Proposed messaging to customer: explain the methodology, attach the workbook and logs, show the calculation, and state issuance timeline (applied to next invoice within 7 business days, credit note attached).

I'll draft the customer-facing note; Karthik, once you confirm the issuance mechanism I'll attach the signed PDF and route to billing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Escalations Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Alice / Quantaforge billing team —

Thanks again for reporting the Aug 8 throughput degradation. Per the attached workbook and our review, here is the formal determination and proposed remedy under Section 4.2 of your SLA: 

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2026-08-08T02:20:00Z — 2026-08-08T14:30:00Z (12.17 hours)
- Calculated unserved-equivalent hours (60% shortfall): 7.30 hours
- Gross pro-rata credit (7.30 / 720 * $180,000): $1,825.20
- Contractual degraded-throughput cap (50% of gross): $912.60

Proposed remedy:
- Issuance: Account credit in the amount of $912.60.
- Form: credit note (PDF attached: redwood_credit_note_QF-2026-0894.pdf) and a ledger entry applied to your next invoice.
- Timeline: credit will be applied within 7 business days after your written acceptance.

Attachments included: quantaforge_throughput_logs.csv; credit_calc_workbook.xlsx; redwood_credit_note_QF-2026-0894.pdf

If you prefer an invoice adjustment instead of an account credit, we can route that to Finance and it will add ~2–3 business days to the timeline. Let me know which you prefer and we'll finalize.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
